los.text: Differentiate between cardiac rhythms that require defibrillation and those that do not, demonstrating accurate rhythm recognition and appropriate decision-making in emergency situations.
los.html:
RhythmShockable?
Ventricular fibrillation (VF)Yes
Pulseless ventricular tachycardia (pVT)Yes
AsystoleNo: CPR, adrenaline 1 mg ASAP
Pulseless electrical activity (PEA)No: CPR, adrenaline, treat reversible causes
4 Hs and 4 Ts(reversible causes)Hypoxia, hypovolaemia, hypo/hyperkalaemia (metabolic), hypothermia; thrombosis (coronary or pulmonary), tension pneumothorax, tamponade, toxins.
ShockableShock, CPR 2 min, after the 3rd shock give adrenaline 1 mg and amiodarone 300 mg; adrenaline every 3–5 min.

los.text: Safely perform defibrillation in accordance with current clinical guidelines, demonstrating correct use of equipment and adherence to safety protocols during resuscitation.
los.html:
Safe defibrillation
Pads: right below the clavicle, left mid-axillary line (V6 position)
Continue compressions while charging
"Stand clear, oxygen away, I'm shocking": check everyone is clear
Deliver the shock (biphasic 120–200 J first, then per device), resume CPR immediately for 2 minutes
Minimise pauses (<5 s); remove oxygen sources; dry chest; remove GTN patches
AED: follow voice prompts

los.text: Perform a thorough clinical examination of the ear, nose, and throat.
los.html:
ENT examination
  • Ear: inspect the pinna and behind the ear (scars, mastoid)
  • Otoscopy (pull the pinna up and back in adults, down and back in children): canal (wax, discharge, otitis externa), tympanic membrane (colour, light reflex, perforation, fluid level, bulging)
  • Hearing: whisper test
  • Rinne's (512 Hz fork: air > bone normal) and Weber's (lateralises to the affected ear in conductive loss, to the good ear in sensorineural loss)
Nose: external shape, septum, nasal patency, anterior rhinoscopy (polyps, Little's area)
Throat: with a torch and tongue depressor: tonsils (size, exudate), pharynx, palate, uvula; neck lymph nodes
Finish: cranial nerves (VII, VIII), flexible nasendoscopy if indicated
